claims.text: Incorporating yttrium oxide nanoparticle dispersoids into refractory high-entropy alloys will improve radiation tolerance.
Incorporating yttrium oxide nanoparticle dispersoids will preserve the mechanical integrity of the alloy.
Yttrium oxide nanoparticle dispersoids can be incorporated by direct addition.
Yttrium doping can form in situ oxide dispersoids during alloy processing.
Neutron irradiation at approximately 500–1000°C and doses up to about 10 dpa represents fusion-relevant irradiation conditions for the proposed application.
The intervention will produce uniformly dispersed yttrium oxide nanoparticles within the alloy microstructure.
Yttrium oxide nanoparticle dispersoids act as sinks for radiation-induced defects.
The dispersoids capture and annihilate radiation-induced point defects and small defect clusters.
Defect capture and annihilation by the dispersoids will reduce radiation-induced defect accumulation.
Defect capture and annihilation by the dispersoids will reduce void swelling.
The modified alloy will have lower radiation-induced defect density than the unmodified baseline.
The modified alloy will have lower radiation-induced void swelling than the unmodified baseline.
The modified alloy will exhibit only a minimal change in yield strength relative to the unmodified baseline.
The modified alloy will exhibit only a minimal change in ductility relative to the unmodified baseline.
Temperature, dose, or processing deviations that compromise nanoparticle dispersion may limit the radiation-tolerance benefit.
The magnitude of defect reduction and mechanical-property retention may vary with processing and irradiation parameters.
